statements.quote: I started writing this before the Administration’s latest “health initiative” that proposes massive involuntary treatment, so it’s even more likely now.
statements.context: Opening section. The author says he began the article before the federal administration's 'health initiative' (executive order on civil commitment) that proposes massive involuntary treatment; 'it' is 'even more likely now'. The referent is ambiguous: more involuntary treatment happening, or the relevance of his critique.
entities: the Administration (federal executive order on civil commitment)
statements.note: Borderline: ambiguous referent of 'it'. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: We have IV Ketamine, Spravato, Accelerated TMS, SAINT TMS, and soon psychedelic treatments.
statements.context: Arguing that a 5-7 day inpatient stay with oral antidepressants cannot work because they take weeks. Lists existing faster-acting treatments and asserts that psychedelic treatments will soon be among them (implying imminent approval or availability).
statements.note: Later in the post the author hedges: 'rapid-acting psychedelics, if approved by the FDA'.

statements.quote: If they treated patients more quickly, they would make less money per patient, since they are paid per day, in 75% of settings..
statements.context: Explains why rapid-acting treatments are almost never available on inpatient psychiatric units: per-diem contracts in 75% of settings mean faster treatment would cut revenue per patient. Conditional economic claim about hospital units under the current payment model.
statements.note: Structural conditional about a hypothetical practice change, not a dated forecast. Borderline.

statements.quote: Which, of course, per the math above, would increase rates of suicide by 0.98% per 10% increase above the baseline rate at which hospitalization would occur in edge cases.
statements.context: Applies the Emanuel et al. (NY Fed Staff Report 1158) estimate to the administration's executive order 'Restoring Civil Commitment': pushing edge-case hospitalization toward 100% would raise suicide/overdose deaths by 0.98 percentage points per 10-point rise in hospitalization propensity.
entities: Emanuel et al. (Federal Reserve Bank of New York)
statements.note: Conditional on the executive order being implemented; numeric extrapolation from a study. Sibling statement on violent crime follows.

statements.quote: When it comes to violent crime, it’s going up by 2.6% per 10% increase in likelihood of admission.
statements.context: Same extrapolation: if the administration's plan raises involuntary admission of edge cases, charges for violent crime within 3 months rise by 2.6 percentage points per 10-point increase in admission likelihood.
entities: Emanuel et al. (Federal Reserve Bank of New York)
statements.note: Conditional numeric extrapolation; sibling of the suicide-rate statement.

statements.quote: We will kill more than just the patients we choose to admit involuntarily, but violence against others is likely to ensue.
statements.context: Conclusion of the extrapolation: if the administration's civil-commitment push is enacted, more involuntarily admitted patients will die and violence against others will follow.
statements.note: Compound: deaths plus violence. Conditional on the policy being implemented.

statements.quote: And, of course, this means that hospitalizing more people against their will—by legal fiat—is a terrible idea, as it will lead to more deaths: At a 100% hospitalization rate, the risk increases to 3.3% for the three months after discharge.
statements.context: Math section (checked with two mathematicians) using a linear model P(Y)=b0+0.022*propensity from Emanuel et al. If the administration's policy pushes edge-case hospitalization to 100%, the 3-month suicide/overdose death risk rises to about 3.3% from a 1.1% baseline, an 'Adjusted Average Administration Harm' of about 2.3%.
statements.horizon_text: for the three months after discharge
entities: Emanuel et al. (Federal Reserve Bank of New York)
statements.note: Compound: policy verdict plus numeric extrapolation. Restates the 0.98%-per-10% claim in absolute terms.

statements.quote: This practice shift will be challenging for all the reasons Awais Aftab highlights—liability is a concern, the optics of that risk are a concern, and more.
statements.context: Closing section. The author calls on clinicians to default to discharge instead of involuntary admission in edge cases and predicts this shift in practice will be difficult because of liability and optics concerns.
statements.note: Prediction about the difficulty of a practice change the author advocates.

statements.quote: But when you change your family routines or “join in” on the avoidance, your child’s anxiety will get worse over time, and the demands to provide yet more FA will only increase.
statements.context: Family accommodation (FA) essay citing Shepherd et al. 2025 and a 2016 OCD meta-analysis. General clinical prediction: parental accommodation of a child's avoidance worsens the child's anxiety over time and increases demands for more accommodation. Not tied to a date or event.
statements.note: General clinical causal claim, not a dated forecast; logged for recall.

statements.quote: This makes me more comfortable with the validity of these results, and thus more excited to pull together an article that won’t make me look dumb a year later if the findings don’t hold up.
statements.context: Meta-article on a Spanish retrospective cohort (Moleón-Ruiz et al., Clinical Neurophysiology 2025; n=104) in which 30 sessions of bilateral DLPFC rTMS reduced suicidal ideation (61% SI remission), with lower baseline anxiety predicting greater SI reduction. Because this matches Siddiqi et al.'s circuit findings, the author expresses confidence the results will hold up.
statements.note: Implicit forecast that the rTMS-for-suicidal-ideation findings will hold up. Borderline.

statements.quote: In summary, I think this scientific paper will make a fine article.
statements.context: Author's judgment about the article he is writing (this newsletter post) on the Moleón-Ruiz rTMS paper.
statements.note: Trivial own-newsletter statement; coder may mark CONTROL or drop.

statements.quote: They include Spravato , Nightware, eTNS, PRISM Neurofeedback, soon, eCOT-AS by Neurolief, TMS , Accelerated TMS, and fMRI-guided SAINT TMS.
statements.context: Closing Radial advertisement listing next-generation treatments at Radial (the author is its CMO) and stating that eCOT-AS by Neurolief (the author is also CMO of Neurolief) will be offered soon.
statements.note: Own organizations (Radial, Neurolief): coder marks CONTROL. Same boilerplate appears in posts 5 and 6 of this packet.

statements.quote: Young people are busy building businesses to be acquired by Pharma. They’re not gonna turn around and decide that the entire Pharma business model is all wrong
statements.context: Footnote 12 on the What If Ventures fellowship and the 2000+ funded mental-health startups: young founders build companies to be acquired by pharma and will not challenge the pharma business model, so startups will not address antipsychotic-driven metabolic harm.
statements.note: Footnote in a 'revisited' repost of an older article; original date not given. Sibling: 'never going to get a company funded'.

statements.quote: You’re never going to get a company funded with that attitude.
statements.context: Footnote 12: a founder who says the entire pharma business model is wrong will never get venture funding; such a stance sounds 'anti-psychiatry'.
statements.note: Negative call; part of a repost of an older article.

statements.quote: “Stable rates of terrible things” is not a phenomenon to count on in 2025, it seems.
statements.context: On Keyes et al. (JAMA Netw Open 2025): murder-suicide rates were about 0.2-0.3 per 100,000 before 2004 and rose to 0.5 in 2022. The author implies rates will not hold stable in 2025, i.e. the rise continues.
statements.note: Borderline: hedged implication of a continued rise; data run only to 2022.

statements.quote: My very strong suspicion is that the only robust healing tools for survivors are likely to be psychotherapy.
statements.context: No published guidance exists for murder-suicide survivors; the author expects psychotherapy, not a drug, to be the only robust healing tool.
statements.confidence_phrase: very strong suspicion; likely to be
statements.note: Belief about what will prove effective; no dated future state. Logged for recall.

statements.quote: However, the benefit to society of bulking up adept therapists is that they might also be able to treat the “emotional distress” of our white male perpetrators, before they do something awful, too.
statements.context: Conditional: if society invests in more skilled therapists for murder-suicide survivors, those therapists might also treat the distress of would-be perpetrators before violence occurs. Hedged.
